paragraphs: Most primary schools in Ireland are religious schools. Nearly nine in ten of them are Catholic. Children learn about the Catholic faith during the school day.
Parents can take their children out of religion classes. This is a right in the Irish Constitution.
But some parents are unhappy. They say their children feel alone and left out. Often the children sit at the back of the room during the class.

Now the Department of Education will write new guidance for schools. It wants schools to treat these children in a fair way. The work will start early in 2027. Parents, teachers and students will give their ideas.
Until then, each school can choose what to do. But every school must help parents who ask.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭大多數小學是宗教學校。
其中將近九成是天主教學校。
孩子們在上學時間學習天主教信仰。
家長可以讓孩子不上宗教課。
這是愛爾蘭憲法賦予的權利。
但有些家長不滿意。
他們說孩子覺得孤單、被排除在外。
上課時，這些孩子常常坐在教室後面。
現在教育部將為學校制定新指引。
它希望學校公平對待這些孩子。
這項工作將在2027年初開始。
家長、老師和學生都會提供意見。
在那之前，每所學校可以自己決定怎麼做。
但每所學校都必須協助提出要求的家長。

paragraphs: The Department of Education is planning new guidelines for schools. They will explain how schools should treat children who do not take part in religion classes.

More than 90% of primary schools in Ireland have a religious ethos, and 88% of these are Catholic. Children learn Catholic teaching during the school day and prepare for First Communion and Confirmation in class. Under the Constitution, parents have the right to take their children out of these lessons.

At the moment, there are no official guidelines on how schools should handle these requests. Some parents say their children feel left out because they often have to sit at the back of the room while the lesson continues.

The Department says each school must help parents who ask for this. It will start talking to parents, teachers, students and school owners in early 2027. It does not keep official records of how many children opt out.

Separately, schools have until Monday to say if they want to be among the first schools to make changes following a survey. About 40% of parents said they want their religious school to welcome all faiths.
sentZh: 教育部正在規劃給學校的新指引。
指引將說明學校應如何對待不上宗教課的孩子。
愛爾蘭超過90%的小學具有宗教辦學理念，其中88%是天主教學校。
孩子們在上學時間學習天主教教義，並在課堂上準備初領聖體和堅振禮。
根據憲法，家長有權讓孩子不上這些課。
目前尚無處理這類要求的官方指引。
有些家長說孩子覺得被排除在外，因為上課時他們常常得坐在教室後面。
教育部表示，每所學校都必須協助提出這項要求的家長。
它將在2027年初開始與家長、老師、學生和學校主辦者對話。
教育部並未保存有多少孩子選擇退出的官方紀錄。
另外，學校須在星期一前表明是否願意成為根據調查結果率先改變辦學安排的學校。
約40%的家長表示，希望自己的宗教學校接納所有信仰。

paragraphs: The Department of Education is to draw up guidance for schools on how to deal with pupils who have been withdrawn from religious instruction, following complaints from parents.

More than 90 per cent of Irish primary schools are run by religious bodies, and 88 per cent of those are Catholic. In these schools, Catholic teaching is part of the school day, and pupils prepare for First Communion and Confirmation in class. The Constitution gives parents the right to opt their children out.

However, there are currently no official guidelines on how schools should handle these requests. Several parents say their children have been isolated, often left sitting at the back of the classroom while religion is taught around them.

The Department says it is committed to developing best-practice guidance. Work will begin in early 2027 with a broad consultation involving patrons, school leaders, parents and students. Until then, each school decides how to manage opt-outs, although all schools are required to facilitate parents' requests. The Department does not keep compulsory records of how many children are withdrawn.

Meanwhile, schools have until Monday to say whether they want to be among the first schools to change their ethos following a national survey, in which about 40 per cent of parents backed a move to multi-denominational education.
sentZh: 教育部將起草指引，說明學校該如何處理被家長要求退出宗教教學的學生，起因是家長的投訴。
愛爾蘭超過百分之九十的小學由宗教團體經營，其中百分之八十八是天主教學校。
在這些學校，天主教教義是上學日的一部分，學生在課堂上準備初領聖體和堅振禮。
憲法賦予家長讓孩子退出的權利。
然而，目前並沒有關於學校應如何處理這類要求的官方指引。
數位家長說，他們的孩子被孤立，常常被留在教室後方坐著，而宗教課就在他們周圍進行。
教育部表示致力於制定最佳做法指引。
工作將於2027年初展開，進行涵蓋主辦團體、學校領導、家長和學生的廣泛諮詢。
在此之前，由各校自行決定如何處理退出事宜，但所有學校都必須配合家長的要求。
教育部並未保存有多少孩子退出的強制性紀錄。
與此同時，學校須在星期一前表明是否願意成為依據全國調查結果率先改變辦學理念的學校；該調查中約百分之四十的家長支持轉為多宗派教育。

paragraphs: The Department of Education is set to devise guidance on how schools should accommodate pupils withdrawn from religious instruction, in response to mounting complaints from parents.

Denominational schools account for more than 90 per cent of the primary sector, and 88 per cent of these are under Catholic patronage. Religious formation is woven into the school day, with preparation for First Communion and Confirmation taking place in the classroom. Parents' entitlement to withdraw their children is enshrined in the Constitution.

Yet no departmental guidelines currently govern how such requests should be handled. A number of parents contend that their children have been marginalised, frequently relegated to the back of the classroom while lessons carry on around them.

The Department insists it is committed to formulating best-practice guidance, with work commencing in early 2027 through an extensive consultation with patrons, management bodies, principals, parents and pupils. In the interim, arrangements remain at each school's discretion, although schools are obliged to facilitate parental requests. Strikingly, no mandatory records of opt-outs are kept.

Separately, Monday marks the deadline for schools to signal whether they wish to be among the first schools to alter their ethos in light of a national survey, in which roughly 40 per cent of parents favoured multi-denominational status.
sentZh: 由於家長的投訴日益增多，教育部將制定指引，說明學校應如何照顧退出宗教教學的學生。
教會學校占小學體系的百分之九十以上，其中百分之八十八由天主教會主辦。
宗教培育融入上學日之中，初領聖體和堅振禮的準備都在教室裡進行。
家長讓孩子退出的權利載於憲法。
然而，目前並沒有部會指引規範這類要求應如何處理。
不少家長主張，他們的孩子被邊緣化，經常被安排到教室後方，而課程就在他們周圍照常進行。
教育部堅稱致力於擬定最佳做法指引，工作將於2027年初展開，透過與主辦團體、管理機構、校長、家長和學生進行廣泛諮詢。
在此期間，相關安排仍由各校自行決定，但學校有義務配合家長的要求。
引人注目的是，目前並未保存任何退出情況的強制性紀錄。
另外，星期一是學校表明是否希望成為依據全國調查結果率先改變辦學理念的學校的截止日；該調查中約百分之四十的家長支持轉為多宗派學校。

paragraphs: The Department of Education intends to develop formal guidance on the treatment of pupils who have been withdrawn from religious instruction, a measure prompted by a substantial number of parental complaints.

Denominational institutions constitute more than 90 per cent of Irish primary schools, and approximately 88 per cent of these operate under Catholic patronage. Consequently, religious instruction is integrated into the daily timetable, and preparation for the sacraments of First Communion and Confirmation occurs during class time. Nevertheless, the Constitution guarantees parents the right to withdraw their children from such instruction.

At present, however, there is no national framework governing how these requests should be managed. Several parents maintain that their children have been socially isolated, often being seated at the back of the classroom while religious lessons proceed around them.

The Department has stated that it is committed to establishing best-practice guidance, beginning with a comprehensive consultation process in early 2027. In the meantime, the implementation of opt-outs is contingent upon the resources of individual schools, although all schools are required to accommodate parental requests. Notably, the Department does not maintain mandatory records of withdrawals.

In a related development, schools must indicate by Monday whether they wish to be among the first schools to modify their ethos following a national survey, in which approximately 40 per cent of parents expressed a preference for multi-denominational education.
sentZh: 教育部打算針對退出宗教教學的學生該如何對待制定正式指引，這項措施是由大量家長投訴所促成的。
教會辦學的機構占愛爾蘭小學的百分之九十以上，其中約百分之八十八由天主教會主辦。
因此，宗教教學被納入每日課表，而初領聖體和堅振禮等聖事的準備也在上課時間進行。
儘管如此，憲法保障家長讓孩子退出此類教學的權利。
然而，目前並沒有全國性的框架規範這些要求該如何處理。
數位家長主張，他們的孩子在社交上被孤立，常被安排坐在教室後方，而宗教課就在他們周圍進行。
教育部表示致力於建立最佳做法指引，將從2027年初的全面諮詢程序開始。
在此期間，退出安排的執行取決於個別學校的資源，但所有學校都必須配合家長的要求。
值得注意的是，教育部並未保存退出情況的強制性紀錄。
在一項相關進展中，學校必須在星期一前表明是否希望成為依據全國調查結果率先調整辦學理念的學校；該調查中約百分之四十的家長表示偏好多宗派教育。
